comments.author: fcollonval
comments.body_normalized:
Testing on binder, it is still not working because actually the server is not sending the correct mimetype for .webp file. See this comparison between the metadata from .webp and .png files:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8435071/189305960-26deef46-7039-4204-8827-330b469c0010.png)

The trouble is that the mimetype is not supported by the Python library `mimetypes` used in Jupyter Server:

https://github.com/jupyter-server/jupyter_server/blob/15310fd760d21be84a1509c0f875970c0c0faaef/jupyter_server/services/contents/filemanager.py#L311

Adding webp was refused because it is not official register as IANA type:
- https://bugs.python.org/issue11362
- https://bugs.python.org/issue45639
- https://bugs.python.org/issue38902

But it got eventually merged recently: https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/29259 - to be released in Python 3.11

I would suggest opening a PR to jupyter server to be able to add additional mimetypes. Ideally through a configurable like `Dict[str, List[str]]` where the keys are mimetypes and the list is all supported extensions; e.g. {'image/webp': ['.webp']}. The mapping will be inverted within the server for quicker look up.

pull_request.author: alec-kr
pull_request.body_normalized:
This commit resolves #12961, by adding support for .webp image files.

## Code changes

<!-- Describe the code changes and how they address the issue. -->
The ```image/webp``` mimeType was added to line 23 of ```jupyterlab/packages/rendermime/src/factories.ts``` to enable MIME support for WebP images in JupyterLab.


## User-facing changes
In issue #12961, users encountered the following error when attempting to add certain .webp files:
![webp-error](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52685467/189016785-db46cbc8-20a7-4960-a565-091cea77a80f.png)

This patch resolves the issue by adding support for WebP files. Hence, users can import these image files, and will no longer be greeted with the error above.
